title: SettingsSection
wrapsNative: Form with Section(content:header:footer:), Toggle, Picker and Button(role: .destructive) rows, toolbar with ToolbarItem(placement: .cancellationAction) and .confirmationAction for Discard and Save, confirmationDialog, and redacted(reason: .placeholder) for loading; MonarchSectionCard for a card on a scrolling page
summary: A recipe, not a component: a titled group of settings as a Form section with a header and a footer, Save and Discard in the toolbar while there are unsaved changes, a danger zone section, and a loading state through redacted.
whenToUse: For a settings screen of grouped options, the way iOS Settings and every system app lay them out. Use the MonarchSectionCard form when settings sit on a scrolling page among other cards, for example on iPad.
whenNotToUse: For a single toggle inside other content, use a Toggle row on its own. For a long form people fill in once, use a Form with MonarchFormField rows and a submit button.
api: Form { Section { Toggle(_:isOn:); Picker(_:selection:content:) } header: { Text(title) } footer: { Text(description) } }
Section { Button(_:role: .destructive, action:) } header: { Text("Danger zone") }
MonarchSectionCard(_:description:content:actions:footer:) with MonarchButton("Save changes", variant: .primary) in the footer

options.name: isDirty
options.description: The draft differs from the saved settings: Discard and Save are enabled.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: The settings are loading: the form is redacted and disabled.

options.name: danger zone
options.description: Destructive actions in their own section, each behind a confirmationDialog.

options.name: no access
options.description: When the person cannot change the settings, disable the controls and say who can in the section footer, or show MonarchEmptyState in place of the form.

states.name: ready
states.description: The sections with their headers, rows and footers; Save and Discard are disabled while nothing has changed.

states.name: dirty
states.description: Save and Discard are enabled in the toolbar; in the card form, "You have unsaved changes." and the two buttons appear in the footer.

states.name: loading
states.description: redacted(reason: .placeholder) draws the rows as placeholders and disabled stops input.

states.name: danger zone
states.description: A section whose button has the destructive role and opens a confirmation.

states.name: no access
states.description: Disabled rows with a footer that says who can change them.

appearance: The system grouped form: section headers and footers in the system's secondary styles, rows on the grouped background, switches and pickers tinted with the accent fill, destructive buttons in the system red. The card form uses the MonarchSectionCard surface and Monarch buttons. Both follow the dark and high-contrast appearances.
platformNotes: The parity map named a MonarchSettingsSectionStyle for Form sections (Android planned a MonarchSettingsSection type and shipped a recipe). Following the native-first rule this is a recipe on iOS as well: SwiftUI has no SectionStyle to customise, and a Form Section already gives the titled group, header, footer, grouped rows, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver order that iOS settings use, so a Monarch style or type would only imitate it. The web's save footer becomes Save and Discard in the toolbar, the iOS pattern for editing screens; the web's sticky footer is not needed because the toolbar stays visible. The web's SettingsRow is a Form row (Toggle, Picker, LabeledContent) and its SettingsActionRow is a Button row. The web's loading skeleton is redacted(reason: .placeholder), and its no-access notice is a footer or MonarchEmptyState. On a scrolling page the web's card look is MonarchSectionCard with the buttons in its footer.
accessibility: Section headers are read as headings by VoiceOver in a Form, and footers are read after their rows.
Toggles and pickers are the system controls, with their roles, values and labels.
Save and Discard are toolbar buttons with text labels and are read as dimmed while disabled.
Destructive actions use the destructive role and confirm before acting.
While loading, the redacted rows are disabled, so nothing can be changed by accident.
edgeCases: Long titles and footers wrap in the Form.
Leaving the screen with unsaved changes should ask first: pair it with the unsaved-changes-guard recipe.
Settings that apply at once (a single switch) need no Save: drop the toolbar buttons.
